newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: LWR SEES FURTHER RATIONALISATION, GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: LWR SEES FURTHER RATIONALISATION, GROWTH.

text.p: Textile manufacturer and distributor LWR Industries Ltd said on Wednesday that there was room for further rationalisation in both the industry generally and LWR specifically.
"LWR's position is strong and directors are expecting to obtain growth in the 1997/98 year," the company said after reporting June year net profit of NZ$8.7 million against $10.3 million a year ago.
Early signs in the new financial year had been very gratifying, LWR said.
LWR said 1996/97 pre-tax profits had been maintained at the previous year's level despite depressed conditions.

"This result is highly credible considering the battering the local manufacturing industry is currently receiving with reducing government tariffs, increasing levels of imports and an extremely high New Zealand dollar throughout the past year.
"Exporting has been difficult, but with a management emphasis on developing overseas markets, sales to customers outside of New Zealand have increased to 39 percent of turnover."

LWR said regretfully, for the New Zealand manufacturing industry, the improved performance had been generated by increased offshore manufacturing, a trend that was likely to increase over coming years.
Consolidated turnover for the year at $147.4 million was down 3.0 percent from the previous year, mainly attributable to the closure of Auckland Knitting Mills and Synthetic Dyeworks.
However, this had been offset by improved sales from new Canterbury of New Zealand operations in South Africa and Europe.
Following the removal of tax grouping arrangements with Brierley Investments Limited, profit after tax profit reduced with the tax charge increasing 57 percent.
LWR said contrary to some media comment its sponsorship arrangement with the New Zealand rubgy union team was not due to expire until 1999 and renewal rights existed.
